analysis_scope.sampling_notes: The repository is small: all tracked files and all seven Python modules were inventoried, with core implementation paths inspected directly. The model and four representative views were read in detail; the remaining sixteen view files were inventoried but not examined field by field. The checkout is shallow at depth 50, so history before the four reachable commits may be unavailable.

stated_purpose: Convert natural-language questions into SQL for a retail LookML schema using retrieval-augmented generation.

observed_capabilities.statement: The command-line entry point supports interactive questions, single-question execution, schema summaries, static question suggestions, statistics, cache clearing, and vector-store rebuilding.

The implementation parses LookML through Gemini, embeds generated schema knowledge through Ollama's nomic-embed-text model, retrieves context from a FAISS index, and asks Gemini to generate, validate, and explain SQL.
The included retail LookML defines 20 views and three explores covering orders, web sessions, and support tickets, with declared joins and analytics measures.
The application persists parsed schema JSON and can persist a FAISS index plus pickled retrieval metadata for reuse.

planned_work.statement: The README lists SQL execution, result visualization, join-path optimization, performance analysis, exports, a web interface, and BI-tool integration as future enhancements.

architecture.statement: main.py is the CLI boundary and constructs TextToSQLGenerator, which coordinates LLMSchemaParser, OllamaEmbeddingModel, FAISSVectorStore, and GeminiLLM.
LLMSchemaParser sends the model and individual view files to Gemini, concurrently processes view files, builds business-term and schema chunks, and caches the resulting structured representation.
Query processing embeds the question, retrieves up to ten schema chunks within a character budget, generates SQL with Gemini, then performs LLM-backed validation and explanation.
The system depends on two separate model runtimes: local Ollama for embeddings and Google's Gemini API for schema parsing and SQL work.

accomplishments.statement: A complete CLI-to-retrieval-to-generation implementation skeleton exists around a substantive sample retail LookML model.
A tracked cache dated 2025-08-19 records successful structured parsing of three explores and 16 views, providing evidence that at least part of the Gemini parsing workflow was exercised.
The seven current Python files parse successfully as Python syntax.
The most recent commit introduced concurrent API use in the schema parser after the preceding Gemini migration.

gaps.statement: There are no automated tests, CI workflows, release tags, deployment artifacts, tracked vector index, or captured end-to-end SQL results.

The tracked cache covers only 16 of the 20 view files; customers, line_items, sessions, and support_tickets are absent even though partial parsing is treated as successful and the unchanged cache can subsequently be accepted.

The README still documents an Ollama Phi3 generator and files named schema_processor.py and llm_model.py, while the current implementation uses Gemini and files named llm_schema_parser.py and gemini_llm.py.
SQL validation is primarily another Gemini prompt, with only shallow fallback checks for SELECT, FROM, and balanced parentheses; no SQL parser or database execution verifies semantic correctness.
The manifest declares google-generativeai while the client imports google.genai and uses genai.Client, so reproducible installation compatibility needs verification.

risks.statement: An incomplete LLM-produced cache can remain valid solely because source hashes match, causing omitted views to be silently excluded from retrieval and generated SQL context.
Generated SQL is not executed or validated against a database, so plausible-looking output may reference incorrect joins, fields, or dialect behavior.
The workflow sends full LookML contents and generated SQL context to an external Gemini service, which may require data-governance review for private schemas.
The Gemini diagnostic function is coded to display the final four characters of the configured API key, creating avoidable partial credential disclosure in terminal logs.
Pinned 2023-era numerical and FAISS dependencies plus an experimental Gemini model identifier may make setup brittle on current Python environments.

suggested_next_actions.statement: Create a clean-environment smoke test that installs the declared dependencies, initializes both model clients, parses all 20 views, builds the index, and generates one known query.
Make cache creation fail or explicitly record degraded status unless every expected view and explore parses successfully.
Add deterministic parser, retrieval, SQL-extraction, and fallback-validation tests that do not require live model calls, followed by an opt-in integration test for Ollama and Gemini.

Align the dependency package and Gemini API usage, replace the experimental default model with a supported configurable value, and update the README to describe the hybrid Ollama/Gemini implementation.
Remove API-key suffix logging and document that private LookML is transmitted to Gemini before any future use.

questions: Was the prototype ever used successfully to generate SQL beyond the tracked partial schema cache?
Were the four missing cached views rejected by Gemini, rate-limited during concurrent parsing, or intentionally excluded?
Is the hybrid Ollama-and-Gemini design still desired, or should inference be fully local or fully hosted?
Is the sample analytics schema synthetic and approved for transmission to Gemini?
Should this dormant experiment be retained as a reference or archived?

evidence.summary: Supplied snapshot identifies a private main-branch repository with no description, open issues, or open pull requests and a last push on 2025-08-20.
Describes a LookML-aware text-to-SQL RAG CLI, setup and commands, example questions, and seven future enhancements, but still documents the superseded Ollama Phi3 design.
Tracks seven Python modules, one requirements file, one schema cache, a 105-line LookML model, and 20 LookML view files; no tests, workflows, notebooks, packaging, or deployment files were found.
Defines three retail analytics explores and 20 views with joins, dimensions, measures, filters, and analytics table names.
Implements argument parsing, system initialization, interactive and one-shot query modes, schema display, statistics, rebuild, and cache-clearing commands.
Connects Gemini schema parsing and SQL generation to Ollama embeddings and FAISS retrieval, then returns SQL, explanation, and validation data.
Concurrently submits LookML model and view contents to Gemini, converts JSON responses into schema knowledge, builds retrieval chunks, and validates cache reuse using source hashes.
Uses Ollama for nomic-embed-text vectors and an in-process FAISS L2 index with pickled metadata persistence and top-k context assembly.
Wraps Gemini API-key authentication, retries, SQL generation, prompt-based validation and explanation, basic fallback validation, and diagnostic connection tests.
Pins faiss-cpu 1.7.4, ollama 0.3.3, numpy 1.24.3, pandas 2.0.3, and regex 2023.6.3 while declaring google-generativeai >=0.5.0.
Tracked cache dated 2025-08-19 contains three parsed explores and 16 parsed views; customers, line_items, sessions, and support_tickets are missing.
All seven Python files passed AST syntax parsing, but no automated tests, CI, live integration run, tracked vector index, or generated-query fixture exists.
The shallow checkout exposes four commits from 2025-08-17 through 2025-08-20: initial LookML, initial RAG implementation, Gemini migration with a generated cache, and concurrent API parsing.

Environment files, virtual environments, vector indexes, pickle metadata, and logs are ignored; no credential-named tracked file was found. Source requires GEMINI_API_KEY and includes a diagnostic that would print a masked suffix.

confidence.rationale: The architecture and implementation gaps are directly supported by the complete small source tree, LookML, cache structure, and reachable history. Confidence is limited because the credentialed Ollama/Gemini workflow could not be executed, there are no automated verification artifacts, and the checkout contains only shallow recent history.

limitations: No credential values were read, displayed, or tested.
The external-model workflow was not executed, so the tracked cache is the only evidence of prior runtime behavior.
The Git clone is shallow at depth 50 and exposes only four commits.
The supplied GitHub snapshot was not independently refreshed.
Sixteen of the twenty view files were inventoried but not inspected field by field.
